updates.content:
Title: Users may have been unable to access Microsoft Defender for Endpoint public APIs 

User impact: Users may have been unable to access Microsoft Defender for Endpoint public APIs. 

Current status: We’ve investigated a problem with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint in which users may have been unable to access public APIs, and we’ve confirmed that service is now restored. We’ll provide additional information in a closure summary within the “History” section of the “Service health” dashboard shortly.

Title: Users may have been unable to access Microsoft Defender for Endpoint public APIs

User impact: Users may have been unable to access Microsoft Defender for Endpoint public APIs. 

More info: Affected API requests may have failed and returned a 503 Service Unavailable error.

Final status: We've determined that a configuration issue during a planned service migration caused some Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Public API requests to continue being routed to infrastructure that was no longer configured to process those requests, resulting in 503 errors. We've restored service capacity on the affected infrastructure, allowing API requests to process successfully and remediating the impact.

Scope of impact: Impact was specific to some users attempting to access Microsoft Defender for Endpoint public APIs. 

Start time: Thursday, September 24, 2026, at 8:17 AM UTC

End time: Thursday, September 24, 2026, at 10:55 AM UTC

Root cause: A configuration issue during a planned service migration caused some Public API requests to continue being routed to infrastructure that was no longer configured to process those requests, resulting in 503 errors.

Next steps: We’re reviewing our service migration and traffic routing configuration procedures to prevent similar issues from recurring.

This is the final update for the event.
